εἰς or ἐς, PREP. WITH ACC. ONLY:—both forms are found in , Ion. poets, and early metrical Inscrr.; ἐς is best attested in and , and is found in nearly all early Ion. Inscrr. (exc. (Thasos, v B. C.), ib. (Oropus, iv B. C.)); εἰς in Att. Inscrr. from iv B. C., , etc.; and usu. in Att. Prose (exc. ) and Com. (exc. in parody): Trag. apptly. prefer εἰς, but ἐς is used before vowels metri gr.; ἐς was retained in the phrases ἐς κόρακας (whence the Verb σκορακίζω), ἐς μακαρίαν. Aeol. poets have εἰς before vowels, ἐς before consonants, and this is given as the rule in by , cf. ap. (Orig. ἐνς, as in (Argos), (Crete); cf. ἐν, ἰν. The diphthong is genuine in Aeol.εἰς, but spurious in Att.-Ion.) Radical sense
